note: Publication status describes the recorded source of each contribution: unpublished means no paper is recorded for that work. Participant credit is separate from verification, and does not by itself establish global priority. Reproductions are credited as computations of published results. Participant work is credited to the vxvware organisation.

contributions.title: G-matrices at n=49, contradicting a published nonexistence statement
contributions.summary: [@djokovic2018goethals] report a complete classification of cyclic families with symmetric or skew blocks for odd v < 50 and find none of type (kkss) at v=49, where the only parameter set of that type is (49; 24,24,22,18; 39). The vxvware census finds eight quadruples with exactly that parameter set, all in one class under the board's equivalence, and the rows verify exactly on this board. The same program reproduces the published counts at v=33, 37, 41, 43, and 45.

contributions.title: G-matrix censuses at n=51, 55, 57, and 59
contributions.summary: Complete vxvware censuses past the range classified by Đoković and Kotsireas [@djokovic2018goethals]: four classes at n=51, three at n=55, none at n=57, and eight quadruples at n=59 that the source counts as two classes and the board as one. Existence at 51 and 55 was already known from Spence's infinite family [@spence1977skew] (q = 101 and 109); the class counts at 51 and 55, the nonexistence at 57, and the existence and count at 59 are new. Replays with pinned engines between 2026-11-14 and 2026-11-15 returned the same classes at each order, so the four counts are exact. The empty cell at 53 is not a search result: a (kkss) parameter set exists only when 2v - 1 is a sum of two squares, by the parameter-set condition of [@djokovic2018goethals], and 105 is not.

contributions.title: G-matrices at n=61, first existence and two classes
contributions.summary: The exhaustive vxvware gmat_c census at n=61, the first open G-matrix order, found a (kkss) quadruple with row sums (1, 1, -11, -11) in its ninth piece on 2026-10-18 and finished all 32 pieces on 2026-10-22 after 811 cpu-hours: twelve quadruples, two classes under the board's equivalence (three under the source's own convention, which does not transpose blocks). Spence's family [@spence1977skew] does not reach 61, Đoković and Kotsireas [@djokovic2018goethals] classify through 49, and the 2009 table of cyclic families in [@djokovic2009supplementary] leaves type (kkss) open at (61; 30, 30, 25, 25; 49), the only parameter set of that type at 61. The rows verify exactly; the count of two became exact on 2026-11-15, when a replay with the pinned kkss-census-c-v3 engine returned the same classes. The first quadruple keeps its hand-entered id and the census maps its class onto it.

contributions.title: G-matrix census at n=69, empty
contributions.summary: The board's compression census at n=69 (kkss-compress-v1, compression by 3) lifted all 750,638 of its compressed instances and found no G-matrices. The only (kkss) parameter set at 69 is (69; 34,34,31,27; 57), and no published search covers this order: 2v - 1 = 137 is a prime congruent to 1 mod 8, outside Spence's family [@spence1977skew]; [@djokovic2018goethals] classify through v < 50, and the table of [@djokovic2009supplementary] stops at 63. Cyclic difference families with these parameters are constructed in [@djokovic2023skew], but only one of their blocks is skew and only one symmetric, so they are not G-matrices. The nonexistence is exact on the board through the registered replay of the pinned engine.

contributions.title: G-matrix census at n=63
contributions.summary: The board's compression census at n=63 (kkss-compress-v1, compression by 3) lifted all 923,658 of its compressed instances and found 12 classes of G-matrices. Existence at 63 was known from Spence's family [@spence1977skew] (q = 125), with parameters (63; 31,31,27,25; 51); no exhaustive count at this order is published. None has parameters (63; 31,31,29,24; 52), the other (kkss) parameter set at 63, which the table of cyclic families in [@djokovic2009supplementary] leaves open: it has no G-matrices. The count is exact on the board through the registered replay of the pinned engine.

contributions.title: Good matrices at n=53, 55, and 61
contributions.summary: The vxvware census found good matrices at three orders no published search covers: 104 rows at n=53, 40 at n=55, and 120 at n=61, each yielding one class. The rows verify exactly; replays with the pinned good-census-c-v1 engine on 2026-11-14 to 2026-11-16 returned the same classes, so the three counts are exact. At 55 a repository note in a commit dated 2026-10-25 [@kishan2026notes] reports an independent exhaustive classification with exactly one class; it cites this board for existence at 53, 55 and 61. A note published on 2026-11-16 [@kumar2026good5355] prints one set of good matrices at each of orders 53 and 55, each in the board's class at that order, and calls them the first to its knowledge; it does not mention this board, whose rows at both orders were recorded on 2026-10-15.

contributions.title: Good-matrix census at n=59, empty
contributions.summary: Two independent complete runs of the vxvware census report no good matrices at n=59. A full replay with the pinned good-census-c-v1 engine on 2026-11-18 also found none, so the board reproduces the empty census. A note published on 2026-11-16 [@kumar2026williamson75] reports, at the evidence level it calls internal, that its own searches found no good matrices of order 59; it does not mention this board, which has recorded the claim since 2026-10-16.

contributions.title: Orbit-restricted G-matrix search at n=63
contributions.summary: A search with the two skew rows constant on the orbits of the subgroup generated by 4 reproduces the known Spence example [@spence1977skew] at parameters (63; 31,31,27,25; 51). It is not a census and establishes no count.

contributions.title: Independent G-matrix censuses through n=45
contributions.summary: The vxvware census recomputes type kkss at every admissible odd order through 45 and agrees with the class counts published by Đoković and Kotsireas [@djokovic2018goethals] at 33, 37, 41, 43, and 45. The imported rows put exactly verified quadruples in cells that had only a citation.

contributions.title: Best-matrix search at n=73 (unconfirmed)
contributions.summary: Unconfirmed: one GPU search at n=73 in September 2026 found no best matrices. The board does not treat this as established and the cell stays open. An audit found a rounding bug that had dropped one admissible class (since searched, empty), and 104,500 of about 11.2 million classes lack identity receipts. An independent census with a different program is running. If it holds, 73 would be a counterexample to the best matrix conjecture; order 73 was left open in [@bright2019best].

contributions.title: Skew families at n=73
contributions.summary: The vxvware sweep generated 15,360 quadruples, yielding eight verified classes. Published skew-Hadamard existence at order 292, by a construction of Đoković recorded by Cati and Pasechnik [@cati2024database], is credited separately; these are participant-generated families, without a claim of first existence at this order.

contributions.title: Good-matrix nonexistence campaign at n=65
contributions.summary: The campaign reports nonexistence. A missing early receipt chain leaves this an archived claim, with participant credit retained. A repository note in a commit dated 2026-10-25 [@kishan2026notes] reports an independent exhaustive search of 67,437 compressed instances that found no good matrices of order 65; it describes this board's claim as unverified. A note published on 2026-11-16 [@kumar2026williamson75] reports the same at the evidence level it calls internal and does not mention this board, whose claim was recorded on 2026-10-14.

contributions.title: Good-matrix partial search at n=67
contributions.summary: Participant search with partial coverage from the withdrawn first run; it does not establish nonexistence. The complete census that does is recorded separately as good-67-empty.

contributions.title: Row-sum obstruction for one restricted family at n=89 (order-11 coset unions)
contributions.summary: Rules out one restricted family at n = 89 only: quadruples with a skew block whose four blocks are unions of cosets of the order-11 multiplier subgroup, by their row sums. The verified quadruples at n = 89 lie outside it.

contributions.title: Independent good-matrix computation at n=41
contributions.summary: An independent campaign for the nonexistence result of Bright, Đoković, Kotsireas and Ganesh [@bright2019good]. The archived run records pass the board's checks; the board has not rerun the GPU search.

contributions.title: Independent best-matrix censuses through n=43
contributions.summary: The vxvware exact census implementation independently enumerates the small orders classified by Bright, Đoković, Kotsireas and Ganesh [@bright2019best]. The board reports exact counts only when its full replay succeeds.

contributions.title: Skew quadruple at n=119
contributions.summary: A cyclic skew quadruple of order 119, giving a skew-Hadamard matrix of order 476, posted on 2026-10-23 in a public repository [@kishan2026hadamard] with no accompanying paper. Imported from its certificate; the discovery is the repository author’s.

contributions.title: Published constructions and catalogue imports
contributions.summary: Imported reference constructions retain the original source attribution. Inclusion in the challenge catalogue does not make the importer their discoverer. The Williamson entries include every class of Holzmann, Kharaghani and Tayfeh-Rezaie [@holzmann2008williamson] through order 59, and both classes at 63 and the Turyn class [@turyn1972infinite] at 69 from the MathCheck enumeration of Bright, Kotsireas and Ganesh [@bright2018enumeration] [@bright2020williamson].

contributions.title: Good-matrix census at n=67, empty
contributions.summary: The re-run of the vxvware census with the corrected wide-word engine, validated against the stored n=37 census before every shard and run as sixteen resumable shards on two hosts from 2026-10-27 to 2026-11-10, reports no good matrices at n=67 after 11.76e12 triples. The board records the attributed claim without a verification tier because the search has not been replayed here.

contributions.title: Skew quadruples at n=65, 67, 69 and 71 by pool join
contributions.summary: One quadruple with a skew block at each of n=65, 67, 69 and 71, found on 2026-11-19 by the sampling search in research/starter/skew: the skew block is fixed in advance, invariant under a multiplier subgroup of odd order, and the other three blocks are sampled inside per-lag autocorrelation windows and joined exactly. The skew-Hadamard orders 260, 268, 276 and 284 are not among the open orders of baselines/skew-gaps.json; these are the board's first quadruples with a skew block at those n, without a claim of first existence. Quadruples with a skew block over the cyclic group were already published at all four orders: constructions of 1992 at 65 and 67 are recounted in [@djokovic1994five], 69 is in [@djokovic2023skew], and 71 belongs to the family of [@xia2005infinite] for prime powers q = 4n - 1 (q = 283). The search is not a census and says nothing about how many classes exist.

contributions.title: Skew quadruples at n=93, 95, 97 and 113 by orbit search
contributions.summary: One quadruple with a skew block at each of n=93, 95, 97 and 113, found on 2026-11-20 by the orbit-restricted searches in research/starter/skew: all four blocks are constant on the orbits of a multiplier subgroup of odd order (5, 9, 3 and 7). The quadruples at 93, 95 and 113 come from the exhaustive search of that orbit space (complete at 95 and 113, stopped at the tenth solution at 93), the one at 97 from the pool join restricted to it. The skew-Hadamard orders 372, 380, 388 and 452 are not among the open orders of baselines/skew-gaps.json; these are the board's first quadruples with a skew block at those n, without a claim of first existence. Quadruples with a skew block over the cyclic group were already published at all four orders: constructions of 1992 at 93 and 113 are recounted in [@djokovic1994five], 95 belongs to the family of [@xia2005infinite] for prime powers q = 4n - 1 (q = 379), and 97 is in [@djokovic2008skew]. The searches cover one orbit space each and are not a census of the cells.

contributions.title: Skew quadruples at n=77, 103, 105, 109, 111, 117, 121 and 123 by orbit-restricted pool join
contributions.summary: One quadruple with a skew block at each of n=77, 103, 105, 109, 111, 117, 121 and 123, found on 2026-11-20 by the pool join of research/starter/skew restricted to quadruples in which all four blocks are constant on the orbits of a multiplier subgroup: order 3 at 77, 103, 105, 109, 111 and 117, order 5 at 121 and 123. The skew block and the row sums are fixed by the plan; the runs at 77 and 109 found one solution each, the run at 105 two, the others between 7 and 86. The skew-Hadamard orders 308, 412, 420, 436, 444, 468, 484 and 492 are not among the open orders of baselines/skew-gaps.json; these are the board's first quadruples with a skew block at those n, without a claim of first existence. Quadruples with a skew block over the cyclic group were already published at all eight orders: 77, 105, 111, 117 and 123 belong to the family of [@xia2005infinite] for prime powers q = 4n - 1 (q = 307, 419, 443, 467 and 491), 103 is in [@djokovic1994five], which also recounts a construction of 1992 at 121, and 109 is in [@djokovic2008orders]. The searches are samples of one orbit space each and are not a census of the cells.

contributions.title: Skew quadruples at n=83 and 125 from the Paley matrices
contributions.summary: One quadruple with a skew block at each of n=83 and 125, in the form A skew, B symmetric, C = D that [@xia2005infinite] proves to exist for every prime power q = 4n - 1 (q = 331 and 499). The rows were generated on 2026-11-21 from the Paley matrices [@paley1933orthogonal] of orders 332 and 500 by the script recorded in evidence/literature/paley-four-circulant.txt; they were not transcribed from the source. These are literature constructions, not new results and not search results, and the credit is the source's. The board had no quadruple with a skew block at those n before.

contributions.title: Skew quadruple at n=81 over the cyclic group by compression search
contributions.summary: One quadruple with a skew block at n=81 over the cyclic group Z_81, found on 2026-11-21 by a search that fixes the skew block and the 3-compressions of the other three blocks, enumerates every lift of each compressed block, keeps the lifts whose periodic autocorrelations lie in five-value windows, and joins the three pools exactly. The search code is not in the repository; the run record is evidence/participants/compression/skew-81.txt. A skew-Hadamard matrix of order 324 has been known since 1994, from supplementary difference sets in the elementary abelian group of order 81 [@djokovic1994five]; the order is not new and is not among the open orders of baselines/skew-gaps.json. The board's entry is over the cyclic group. A search of current sources on 2026-11-21 found no earlier quadruple with a skew block over Z_81; that is a report of the search, not a proof of priority, and no first existence is claimed. This is the board's first quadruple with a skew block at n=81. The join stopped at its first solution, so the search is a sample and not a census.

contributions.title: Williamson census at n=65, empty, confirming earlier public records
contributions.summary: The board's compression census at n=65 lifted all 72,478 of its compressed instances and found no Williamson matrices; the census entry is dated 2026-11-14. Two public records are earlier and report the same result: a Zenodo preprint whose version 1 is dated 2026-10-22 [@graham2026williamson65], and a repository note in a commit dated 2026-10-25 [@kishan2026notes]. Neither is peer reviewed. The board's run is an independent confirmation, not a first result. Each of the earlier records counts 70,699 compressed instances against the board's 72,478; the difference has not been reconciled.

contributions.title: Williamson census at n=67, empty
contributions.summary: The board's census at n=67 (williamson-hkt-v3) covered all 7 row-sum decompositions of 268 in six groups, sent about 2.27e13 row pairs to its linear solver with no nullity-capped system, and found no Williamson matrices. Published classifications stop below this order: [@holzmann2008williamson] classify the odd orders through 59, and [@bright2020williamson] enumerate the odd orders divisible by 3 below 70, which are 63 and 69. The repository of the order-65 preprint [@graham2026williamson65] describes order 67 as open. A search of the literature and of public repositories on 2026-11-24 found no claim at 67 in either direction. This is a single run of one engine; the nonexistence is exact on the board through the registered replay of the pinned engine.

contributions.title: Good-matrix census at n=75, empty, confirming an earlier report
contributions.summary: The board's two-divisor compression census at n=75 (good-compress2-v1, compression by 5 and by 3) lifted all 1,612,793 of its compressed instances of length 15, in 3,137 signature groups, and found no good matrices; the census entry is dated 2026-11-25. The result was reported earlier: a note published on 2026-11-16 [@kumar2026williamson75] states that an exhaustive computer search found no circulant good matrices of order 75. The note is not peer reviewed, publishes neither its method nor a certificate, and lists the nonexistence as not established. The board's census was run with the board's own program and agrees with it, so it is an independent confirmation, not a first result. Peer-reviewed searches stop below this order: [@djokovic2018goethals] classify the odd orders below 50, and [@bright2019good] enumerate the odd orders divisible by 3 below 70, of which 75 is the next. Orders 65, 71 and 73 are still open on the board (65 carries an archived nonexistence claim), and its empty cells at 63, 67 and 69 rest on a cited search or on a participant run with no verification tier, so 75 does not extend a complete classification. This is a single run of one engine. The engine returned the board's classes at orders from 45 to 63, where n/(d1 d2) is 1 or 3; at 75 it is 5, and no order with that value has a positive control. The nonexistence is exact on the board through the registered replay of the pinned engine.

contributions.title: Williamson census at n=61, one class, reproducing a published classification
contributions.summary: Lang and Schneider [@lang2012turyn] report in their introduction that they implemented the exhaustive algorithm of Holzmann, Kharaghani and Tayfeh-Rezaie [@holzmann2008williamson], extended its results from order 59 to order 61, and found exactly one equivalence class of Williamson matrices of order 61, which is of Turyn type; Bright, Kotsireas and Ganesh [@bright2020williamson] cite the enumeration at 61 to that paper. Only the first two pages of [@lang2012turyn] were read for this record. The board's own census is a full run of the pinned engine williamson-hkt-v2 on 2026-11-14 (17,359 s on 8 threads), registered as a replay: it returned one class, the Turyn-type quadruple already on the board, so the board's count agrees with the published one. The run is an independent reproduction of a published classification, not a first result.

contributions.title: Eleven skew quadruples at n=89: a skew-Hadamard matrix of order 356
contributions.summary: Eleven skew quadruples at n = 89, found on 2026-11-22 and 2026-11-23 (UTC) by a search that fixes one skew block and joins pools of candidate rows for the other three. Each gives a skew-Hadamard matrix of order 356, the smallest order listed as open in [@djokovic2023skew], [@araya2024classification] and [@egan2026recent], and already listed as unknown in [@wallis1970configurations]. A search of these sources, of the census [@djokovic2025census], which lists v = 89 among the odd v below 2500 with a skew-Hadamard matrix of order 4v undecided, and of the note [@kumar2026skew] with its repository [@kishan2026skew], which give skew-Hadamard matrices for 106 of the values in that census and none of order 356, found no earlier one. Two tables read on 2026-11-26 agree: the table in [@koukouvinos2008skew] of the least t for which a skew-Hadamard matrix of order 2ᵗm is known, for odd m below 500, and the table in [@seberry2020hadamard], for odd q up to 999, both give t = 4 for 89, which is order 1424, and neither has order 356. This does not claim priority, and the result has not been reviewed.

contributions.title: A symmetric Hadamard matrix of order 260, from a propus difference family in Z_65
contributions.summary: Four rows of length 65 that give a symmetric Hadamard matrix of order 260 built from circulant blocks. They form a propus difference family in the cyclic group Z_65: a quadruple (A, B, B, D) with A symmetric, whose propus array [@seberry2015propus] [@balonin2017construction] is a symmetric Hadamard matrix. The published sources have no propus family at 65: [@djokovic2022symmetric] states the conjecture that propus families exist, reports it verified for odd v up to 63 and lists v = 65 as the smallest v for which a symmetric Hadamard matrix of order 4v is undecided, and [@djokovic2023skew] names 65, 89 and 93 as the only odd v below 100 for which none was known and constructs four at v = 93, which leaves 65 and 89. Order 260 has one earlier matrix, by a different construction: a bordered propus array over Z_64 with no circulant blocks of order 65, posted on 2026-10-18 in a repository that is not peer reviewed [@kishan2026symmetric260]; the notes of that repository report that its searches for propus families over Z_65 with multiplier symmetry found none [@kishan2026propus]. The family has row sums 9, 7, 7, 9 and parameters (65; 28, 29, 29, 28; 49), one of the four propus parameter sets at v = 65; B and D are not symmetric and have no multiplier symmetry. It was found on 2026-11-24 by a search that takes every symmetric row of one row sum for A and joins pools of candidate rows for B and D. The search is not a census and does not settle the conjecture at v = 65. A search of the literature and public repositories on 2026-11-24 found no earlier propus difference family in Z_65; this reports the search and does not claim priority, and the result has not been reviewed. The verifier checks only the rows, whose Goethals–Seidel array is a Hadamard matrix that is not symmetric.

contributions.title: A symmetric Hadamard matrix of order 988, from four rows on the cyclic group of order 247
contributions.summary: Four rows of length 247 that give a symmetric Hadamard matrix of order 988. The rows live on the cyclic group of order 247, which the search wrote as Z_13 × Z_19, pairs (x1, x2) of an integer modulo 13 and an integer modulo 19. In the rows as found, one row is unchanged by the map (x1, x2) ↦ (−x1, x2), one is unchanged by (x1, x2) ↦ (x1, −x2), and the other two are carried to each other by (x1, x2) ↦ (x1, −x2); all four are fixed by a group of 9 multipliers. The symmetric matrix is not the Goethals–Seidel array of the rows. It comes from a variant of the propus array [@seberry2015propus] [@balonin2017construction] in which the two equal blocks of that array are replaced by two different blocks tied by the map above. The variant was worked out for this board on 2026-11-25 and is not taken from a published source; the entry page states it with an argument that has not been reviewed, and the claim rests on the build, which rebuilds the matrix from the rows and checks exactly that it is symmetric and Hadamard. What was read about the order on 2026-11-25: the census [@djokovic2025census], a preprint whose file is dated 28 May 2025, lists v = 247 among the 595 odd v below 2500 for which a symmetric Hadamard matrix of order 4v is undecided. For the series of that census, 2v − 1 = 493 = 17 × 29 and 4v − 1 = 987 = 3 × 7 × 47 are not prime powers, 2v is not of the form 1 + (q + 2)q² or 1 + 5 × 9^k, and v is not a fourth power. The one later paper on new symmetric orders that the search found, [@djokovic2025orthogonal], gives orders q(q + 1), and 988 is not of that form; [@egan2026recent] has no list of symmetric orders. A repository that is not peer reviewed holds symmetric Hadamard matrices of 103 orders, without 988 [@kishan2026symmetric]; its notes report searches for propus families at v = 247, exhaustive within three multiplier groups of order 9, one of them the group that fixes these rows, that found none [@kishan2026exhaustive]. Plain web queries for a symmetric Hadamard matrix of order 988 found nothing. The table of known symmetric Hadamard matrices in [@seberry2020hadamard], read on 2026-11-26, lists odd q up to 399 with the least t for which a symmetric Hadamard matrix of order 2ᵗq is known, and marks q = 247 as having none known. Other books, the review databases and pages that are not indexed were not read. The rows were found by an exact join over rows constant on the orbits of the maps above. The run record reports 52,128 solutions, all with row sums 25, 11, 11, 11, among 20 feasible patterns of row sums, in 279 seconds on a laptop; the search is exhaustive for that one choice of maps and says nothing about any other. To our knowledge no symmetric Hadamard matrix of order 988 was known; this reports the search and does not claim priority, and the result has not been reviewed. The verifier checks only the rows, whose Goethals–Seidel array is a Hadamard matrix that is not symmetric.

A repository that is not peer reviewed holds symmetric Hadamard matrices of 103 orders, without 1068 [@kishan2026symmetric]; its notes report searches for propus families at v = 267, exhaustive within one multiplier group, of order 11, the group that fixes these rows, that found none [@kishan2026exhaustive]. Plain web queries for a symmetric Hadamard matrix of order 1068 found nothing. The table of known symmetric Hadamard matrices in [@seberry2020hadamard], read on 2026-11-26, lists odd q up to 399 with the least t for which a symmetric Hadamard matrix of order 2ᵗq is known, and marks q = 267 as having none known. Other books, the review databases and pages that are not indexed were not read. The rows were found by an exact join over rows constant on the orbits of the maps above. The run record reports 14,400 solutions with row sums 1, 23, 23, 3 and 33,120 with row sums 3, 23, 23, 1, the two feasible patterns, in 21 seconds on a laptop; the search is exhaustive for that one choice of maps and says nothing about any other. To our knowledge no symmetric Hadamard matrix of order 1068 was known; this reports the search and does not claim priority, and the result has not been reviewed. The verifier checks only the rows, whose Goethals–Seidel array is a Hadamard matrix that is not symmetric.
